findings.text: A host bus write dispatch is available that takes a vCPU context together with a bus selector, guest address, length and source bytes, signals an absent bus table as a memory failure, and otherwise normalizes a successful device match to success while preserving device layer failures.

A host bus read dispatch is available that takes a vCPU context together with a bus selector, guest address, length and destination buffer, signals an absent bus table as a memory failure, and otherwise normalizes a successful device match to success while preserving device layer failures.

Reverse map fault handling has two dossier visible forms sharing one name, a full handler that validates private state and may split large entries and invalidate mappings, and an empty inline form that accepts the same arguments and performs no action for builds without that feature.

A nested paging fault exit entry consumes hardware provided error and address information, applies synthetic bit sanitation and feature specific adjustments, consults the memory management fault service, optionally invokes reverse map repair on relevant successes, and returns the service outcome to the exit dispatcher.

Three synchronous exit entries report handled status to the dispatcher, one counting external interrupt exits, one routing register exits by direction indication toward read or write emulation, and one requesting event processing while clearing the virtual interrupt window and counting window exits.

Guest memory mapped input output is transferred in bounded pieces of at most eight bytes, and both emulated exit preparation and host dispatch observe the same upper bound when fragmenting longer requests.

When the local interrupt controller is emulated in the kernel, its device is attempted before the generic memory mapped bus for each piece, and the generic bus is consulted only if that attempt is unavailable or declines.

Bus dispatch distinguishes absent bus table, no matching range entry, and no overlapping device accepting the access, with the latter cases surfacing as operation not supported to the memory mapped layer which then stops further progress.

Device lookup locates one overlapping range entry by ordered search and then retreats to the lowest indexed overlapping entry, so subsequent linear scanning starts at the first candidate for the requested address and length.

Overlapping bus devices are tried in increasing index order and dispatch stops at the first acceptance, returning that position internally, while exhaustion without acceptance yields operation not supported.

Bus table acquisition uses sleepable read copy update dereference accompanied by a barrier after read lock acquisition, ensuring that bus table updates observed by an earlier virtual CPU step remain visible to the step that triggered the lookup.
Diagnostic dumping of virtual machine control state is serialized by a scoped mutex guard held for the duration of the dump, preventing interleaved output from concurrent dump attempts.
The bus matching key is a pair of guest address and length that is constructed fresh for each dispatch and compared for overlap against stored per device ranges during search and linear scan.

An emulated access exit toward userspace carries a length, a direction flag, an exit reason identifying memory mapped input output, a guest physical address, and a data area that is populated from the source only for writes.

Observed virtual machine control state includes a control area with exit code and two exit information words plus interrupt and event injection fields and nested and virtual interrupt controls, alongside a save area with segment descriptors, control and debug registers, instruction pointer and flags, stack and general state, privilege level and extended feature state.

Memory mapped handling makes monotonic progress over the requested byte count, advancing the guest address and host pointer by the size of each accepted piece and reporting total accepted bytes, halting on the first declined piece and leaving the remainder unhandled.

Nested fault outcomes depend on fault class and guest mode, with reserved faults outside guest mode eligible for an expedited path that may skip the faulting instruction after a successful zero length fast bus probe, while other faults flow to tracing and memory management resolution with conditional reverse map repair.

Instruction emulation permission is governed by guest confidentiality mode and decode availability, allowing unrestricted emulation without that mode, refusing with retry when register state is hidden, permitting completion when decoding is already done, and otherwise requiring a non empty prefetched instruction buffer with defined fallback faults when absent.

Reverse map repair proceeds through validation of private status and slot capability and backing page presence and table assignment, treats an already small mapping as complete, otherwise attempts a large entry split with tolerance for a concurrent split race, invalidates the affected guest frame range on the split path, records a trace, and releases the backing reference.
Exit preparation enforces the eight byte bound as a fatal kernel invariant while the fragment wrapper clamps larger fragments down to that bound and warns if invoked without pending fragmented state.

Hardware error bits that collide with hypervisor defined synthetic flags trigger a one time warning and are cleared before further handling, and read handling emits distinct tracing for satisfied pieces versus leftover unsatisfied length.

Two hardware errata receive explicit handling, guest mode fetch indication is corrected using current privilege level when a specific control bit is enabled, and empty decode assistance under address space protections is distinguished from genuine fetch or page table faults before choosing between guest fault injection, triple fault request, or guest retry.

Unexpected reverse map conditions such as non private ranges, slots without private memory support, missing backing pages, or unassigned table entries produce rate limited warnings and early return without table modification or mapping invalidation.

Control block dumping is disabled by default behind a module parameter that only emits a hint when disabled, and confidential guests with encrypted save areas require successful save area decryption before register display, otherwise register output is skipped.

The fragments observe distinct bus selectors for normal memory mapped dispatch and for zero length fast probing, a dedicated exit reason identifying memory mapped exits to userspace, and distinct trace points for writes, satisfied reads, unsatisfied reads, fast probes, page faults and reverse map faults.

The fragments observe page fault error bit names for synthetic, reserved, fetch, user, encryption, private and reverse map size conditions, emulation type bits distinguishing fault completion without decode and skip behavior, plus named exit, vector and request identifiers for event vectoring, undefined and protection faults and triple fault.
Virtual CPU page mapping for a guest frame number is provided as a thin inline that forwards to a fuller helper with a fixed truthful final argument and returns that helper status unchanged.

Current privilege level is read directly from the save area, register access direction is decided by the first exit information word, and interrupt related exits maintain dedicated counters while the window variant additionally requests event handling and clears the virtual interrupt indication.
